facts.text: I can hardly open my mouth since my injury and operations.
I was shot in the face and needed life-saving surgery and reconstruction.
The hole in the roof of my mouth was repaired using a flap from my tongue.
My jaw was shattered near the joint, and the broken pieces were set in an operation.
After that, my left jaw joint was replaced with an artificial joint.
I was referred here for rehabilitation to help me open my mouth again.
It's only ever on the left side, around my eye and in my temple.
There's a background ache all the time that gets better and worse.
On top of that I get severe flare-ups that come unpredictably.
During the flare-ups my left eye waters.
During the flare-ups my nose keeps running.

facts.text: I have a burning, tingling feeling over my left cheekbone.
My left eyebrow sits lower and the left side of my forehead is flat.

findings.name: facial sensory examination
findings.result: Allodynia and hyperalgesia in the distribution of the zygomatic branch of the left trigeminal nerve.

gold.reasoning: 1. Cluster headache — considered because of unilateral periorbital pain with autonomic features but excluded because cluster headache attacks are episodic rather than continuous: “with the exception of HC, in that they are typically episodic; HC is an uncommon, benign unilateral and continuous headache, with superimposed exacerbations of severe pain and autonomic features.” 2. Odontalgia — considered because trigeminal autonomic cephalgias often present as dental pain but excluded when ocular autonomic signs and continuous headache were identified: “Cluster headache (CH), chronic paroxysmal hemicrania (CPH) and HC often mimic anterior maxillary odontogenic pain leading to inappropriate dental procedures.” 3. Temporomandibular disorders and trigeminal neuralgia — considered due to masticatory pain and facial sensory changes but excluded because the pain was continuous with autonomic features rather than paroxysmal or movement‐related: “Differential diagnoses also considered in this, and similar cases are temporomandibular disorders and trigeminal neuralgia.” 4. Hemicrania continua — supported by the continuous unilateral headache with superimposed exacerbations and ipsilateral cranial autonomic features and the exclusion of other trigeminal autonomic cephalgias.

source_issues: No response to indomethacin is reported, although an absolute indomethacin response is part of the diagnostic criteria for hemicrania continua.
No vital signs, imaging or other tests are reported.
notes: Index visit: the initial rehabilitation evaluation after the facial gunshot surgery, at which he reported the headache as a second complaint (s001-s011). Both the mouth-opening problem and the headache are in the opening so that the headache is not hidden.
s003: the improvement of the interincisal opening to 28 mm with physical therapy is a treatment response after the index visit and is not used; only the initial 5 mm is a finding.
The ptosis, small pupil and flat forehead could also follow the facial gunshot injury and surgery; the source does not separate them, so they are reported as examined.
The autonomic features of s006 occur during the exacerbations, so they are separate symptom facts tied to the flare-ups (time recurrent).
